dedupe_keys.name: dhis2 open source health information management platform

description: DHIS2 is an open-source platform for collecting, validating, analysing and presenting aggregate and individual-level health data, reported by its developers to be the national health management information system in dozens of countries. It is developed by the HISP Centre at the University of Oslo with a network of regional HISP groups, and is recognised as a digital public good. Ministries of health use it to hold facility registries (the organisation unit hierarchy with facility coordinates), routine service statistics, disease surveillance, immunisation, logistics and stock data, with dashboards, maps, a web API and Android apps for offline data capture. Each country runs its own instance, so data access depends on the ministry, while the software itself is free under the BSD 3-Clause licence, with source code on GitHub and regular core and mobile releases. Caveats: the platform is not a dataset, data quality depends on reporting completeness in each country, and many national instances are closed to the public, although some publish facility lists or indicators. Simulation uses: extracting facility registries and service volumes as inputs to health system capacity planning and accessibility models, feeding surveillance data into epidemic forecasting, and supporting emergency response dashboards. Related records: the Malawi health facility registry extract built from DHIS2 (data-malawi-health-facilities-registry-dhis2) is one published output, and AccessMod (model-accessmod) uses facility lists to model travel time to care.
